Good for Craft Beer Drinkers
Oct 2024 • Couples
Decent sized café-style venue with table seating and lots of retro-beer posters on the walls. They stock only bottles from a range of local not easily available craft and more common international major brewers. The beer list is extensive with limited editions (10 in all from Overmorrow, Labtory, Heart of Darkness, Mixtape; VND110-140000), commercial (8 in all from Vietnam, Laos, Mexico, Japan, Slovakia; VND50-100000), local craft brewers (16 in all from Ha Noi & Saigon; VND100-140000 for 330ml bottle), Belgian (14 in all) and Trappist (7 in all). Prices listed are a bit expensive for the local scene. Non-beer includes ciders (7) and wine. Didn't try the food which consists of snacks and mains. The service is basic (not with-standing language barriers) however, as staff seem to be more focused on their mobile phones, they don't annoy you. NOT a place for lager drinkers but a great place to visit to taste some hard to get local craft beers!!

Best craft beer selection in Hanoi
Aug 2023 • Couples
Wow, stumbling upon New Gentry in Hanoi was like finding a hidden gem in the craft beer universe! The service was top-notch, and my wife's delight in their French and Italian wines was matched only by the blissful chill they kept them at on that warm evening. Now, let's talk beer – their local craft brews were a delight, although that farmhouse-leaning stout had me scratching my beer-loving head. Maybe an infected batch? But hold on to your mugs, because the real magic happened with their exquisite selection of Belgium beers. Oh, the joy of sipping on a Chimay Blue or the Duvel Triple Hop Citra Belgium IPA – pure liquid nirvana that hit the spot every single time. The food, the cozy setting, and that A++ service sealed the deal – this place is an absolute must-visit. Just remember, it's a tiny haven that fills up fast, so make sure to hop in early. In my books, New Gentry stole the show during our short Hanoi escapade, and it's hands down my favorite spot in the city! 🍻

Decent beer, decent food
May 2019 • Solo
If you're simply looking for a place to try a variety of local Hanoi and Vietnamese beers, then New Gentry Beerhouse checks the box. If you want a fun bar atmosphere with a variety of pub food, there are other places that check those boxes. I had the cuban sandwich and it was OK but seemed hastily slapped together in the kitchen and didn't have the craft and creativity common of Western brewpubs, especially in the modern craft beer era. Still, if you're just looking for a cold beer to escape the Hanoi heat, then this isn't a bad spot.
